newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair makes welfare-to-work his top priority.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair makes welfare-to-work his top priority.

text.p: Prime Minister Tony Blair on Monday underscored his commitment to getting Britons off welfare and into work by promising there would be no "forgotten people" in the society his government wants to build.
Blair chose a run-down housing estate in Southwark, south London, to make his first speech oustide parliament since he was swept to power on May 1, ending 18 years of Conservative rule.
"Just as there are no no-go areas for new Labour so there will be no no-hope areas in new Labour's Britain.
"To be a citizen of Britain is not just to hold its passport, it is to share its aspirations, to be part of the British family," Blair said.

He confirmed that the centrepiece of the government's maiden budget, to be presented to parliament on July 2, would be a 3 billion pound programme to put 250,000 unemployed people back to work, financed by taxing the excess profits of privatised utilties.
"It will be the Welfare to Work budget. This will be the Welfare to Work government," Blair, who never visited a run-down neighbourhood during the election campaign, said.
He called for a "new bargain" between all members of society to forge a "one nation Britain" in which everyone had a stake.

"We should reject the rootless morality whose symptom is a false choice between bleeding hearts and couldn't care less, when what we need is one grounded in the core British values, the sense of balance between rights and duties.

"The basis of this modern civic society is an ethic of mutual responsibility or duty. It is something for something. A society where we play by the rules. You only take out if you put in. That's the bargain," said Blair, who discussed welfare reform at length last week with U.S. President Bill Clinton.
He said the government, in drawing up ambitious plans to reform Britain's 90 billion pound a year welfare state, would not fall into the trap of short-termism.

Ministers would be pragmatic in their approach, finding out what works and stopping the policy failures. "We will back anyone -- from a multinational company to a community association -- if they can deliver the goods," Blair said.
"This is a government with a new sense of purpose. A government that believes in giving everyone the chance to succeed and get on in life. It is a government that has a will to win.
"To those who have lost hope over the last 18 years, I offer them a fresh start. The best thing my government can offer is hope, and that is what I bring today," he added.
